title: Philippines transfers ASEAN chairship to Singapore
summary: The Philippines on Tuesday formally handed over the chairship of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) regional bloc to Singapore.

blocks.text: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr speaks during the opening ceremony of the 49th ASEAN Summit at the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City on Sunday, November 15, 2026. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez/Pool
The Philippines on Tuesday formally handed over the chairship of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) regional bloc to Singapore.
This transpired during the closing ceremony of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits in Manila, which was attended by several regional and world leaders.
Philippine President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. led the turnover ceremony, together with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong.
As the new chair, Singapore is set to lead ASEAN in 2027, which coincides with the regional bloc's 60th anniversary.
Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro also previously said the finalization of the long-awaited South China Sea Code of Conduct may be done during the chairship of Singapore.
This came after Southeast Asian nations and China completed negotiations on 80% of the proposed code of conduct as of this year. — VDV, GMA News
